To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
selenium supplementation has no influence on the immune response in patients with asthma.

1. selenium supplementation in asthmatics with corticoid-dependent asthma has no influence on the number of CD3+ cells, CD4+ cells, and CD8+ cells in the peripheral blood; 2. selenium supplementation in the asthmatics with a history of corticoid therapy increases the percentage of CD4+ cells in the blood; and 3. selenium supplementation in patients with corticoid therapy decreases the level of IgE.
selenium supplementation of corticoid-treated asthmatics is beneficial for the patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of selenium supplementation in the form of L-selenomethonine on the immune system in asthmatics.
the influence of the administration of selenium on the immunological status in asthmatic patients with corticoid-dependency.
the influence of selenium supplementation (200 µg/day) on the immune system of corticoid-treated asthmatics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the present study indicate that the supplementation of selenium is beneficial to the immune system of corticoid-treated asthmatics, and that the supplementation may be of value in the management of asthmatics who have to be on long term steroid therapy.
the use of selenium supplementation in asthmatics is beneficial in reducing the severity of asthma attacks and improving lung function, but not in the prevention of asthma attacks.
selenium supplementation is of no value in the treatment of asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
selenium supplementation has no influence on the immunity of asthmatics.
selenium supplementation in asthmatics with corticosteroid dependency is not only safe, but also improves immune function.
selenium supplementation in patients with asthma and corticoid dependence improves their immunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
selenium is not a safe or effective treatment for asthma, and it may actually be dangerous.
selenium supplementation can improve the immune status and decrease the severity of the disease in asthmatic patients.
selenium supplementation may have beneficial effects in the management of corticoid dependent asthmatics.
